deep.reconstruction:
This is the final printed page (p. 15) of Riemann's posthumously published essay 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Henle & Pfeufer's Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 1867; reprinted in his Gesammelte Werke). It finishes section VI on the statics of the malleus; there is no calculation on the page.

Setting (from p. 14): the tendon of the tensor tympani pulls on the malleus at its insertion point. Part of this pull is balanced by the fixation of the handle (manubrium) in the eardrum (Paukenfell) and of the eardrum in the sulcus tympanicus. However, the attachment of the membrane to the handle reaches only a little above the tendon insertion (per v. Tröltsch and Gerlach), and its upper end already lies above the ends of the sulcus. So the sulcus fixation alone cannot balance the muscle.

Condition stated on this page: treat the malleus as a rigid body turning about an axis through, or near, the insertion region. For equilibrium, the net torque must vanish. In my modern notation, with M_below the moment of the forces on the handle below the insertion point and M_above the moment of the forces on the part above it:
  M_above + M_below = 0, i.e. M_above = -M_below.
The forces on the upper part must therefore supply a moment equal in size and opposite in sense to that on the handle.

Riemann lists three candidate sources of this balancing moment:
(1) the connection of the eardrum with the superficial skin layers of the external auditory canal;
(2) the action of the posterior tympanic pouch (hintere Paukenfelltasche);
(3) the combined action of two attachments of the malleus head to the tympanic wall: via the incus on one side and via the Lig. superius (Arnold) on the other.

For (3) he gives a qualitative vector argument. The two ligament lines form an angle opening roughly toward the tip of the short process. When both are under tension, their resultant presses that tip against the eardrum. In my notation, with unit vectors e1 and e2 along the two attachments and tensions T1, T2 > 0, the resultant is R = T1 e1 + T2 e2. R lies inside the angle and points along the bisector when T1 = T2. This furnishes the counter-moment about the rotation axis.
errors: No mathematical errors: the equilibrium condition (vanishing net torque) is correct elementary statics.

Option (3) is a qualitative plausibility argument. It is not quantified and gives no lever arms or force magnitudes. The anatomical claims rest on the 1860s literature cited (v. Tröltsch, Gerlach, Arnold).

results.what: Torque-balance condition for the malleus: the moment on the part above the tensor tympani insertion must equal and oppose the moment on the handle below.
results.modern_name: Rigid-body moment equilibrium (statics of the ossicular chain)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical statics (Archimedes/Varignon); applied to the ossicles by Helmholtz (1868) and others

results.what: Three candidate anatomical sources of the balancing moment, including the resultant of the incus attachment and Arnold's superior ligament pressing the short process against the eardrum.
results.modern_name: Suspensory ligament / ossicular support analysis in middle-ear mechanics
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867); Helmholtz's 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells' (1868)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published closing page of Riemann's known essay 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867, in his Werke). It contains only a qualitative statics argument already attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: F1, r1, F2, r2 = symbols('F1 r1 F2 r2', positive=True); solve(Eq(F1*r1 - F2*r2, 0), F2)  # -> F1*r1/r2
checkable.asserts: Torque equilibrium about the axis: the force needed above the insertion point equals F1*r1/r2.

checkable.sympy: a, T = symbols('a T', positive=True); simplify(T*Matrix([cos(a), sin(a)]) + T*Matrix([cos(a), -sin(a)]))  # -> Matrix([2*T*cos(a), 0])
checkable.asserts: Two equal tensions along lines at ±a give a resultant along the bisector of the angle, of magnitude 2*T*cos(a), as invoked for the incus–Arnold ligament pair.

transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image. The faint mirrored text 'Gedruckt bei E. Polz in Leipzig' in the lower half is show-through from the verso, not part of this page's text. The pencil line and the stray mark in the right margin are not text.
